name: Arleigh Burke Flight II destroyer
role: Aegis guided-missile destroyer for air defence, surface warfare, anti-submarine warfare and land strike

serviceWindow.statusNotes: USS Mahan, the first Flight II ship, was commissioned on 14 February 1998 and is in active service as of 2026-03-15.

dimensions.crew: 329 total (32 officers, 27 chief petty officers, 270 enlisted), the Navy class figure

propulsionSummary: Four General Electric LM2500 gas turbines drive two shafts for about 100,000 shaft horsepower.

weapons.name: RIM-66M SM-2MR
weapons.mountSummary: Fired from the Mk 41 vertical launch system (90 cells on the Flight II ship, shared with Tomahawk and ASROC). The 93 km engine range is a Sandkasten abstraction. The Navy fact file gives SM-2 Medium Range as up to 90 nautical miles (about 167 km), so this row is estimated. Missile count is a typical mix, not a published load.

weapons.name: RGM-84 Harpoon
weapons.mountSummary: Two quad launchers (8 missiles) on the Flight II ship per the ship article. The Navy fact file gives Harpoon range as over 67 nautical miles (about 124 km), so the 139 km engine range is estimated.

weapons.name: Mk 15 Phalanx CIWS
weapons.mountSummary: 20 mm six-barrel gun, 3,000 to 4,500 rounds per minute, one mount in the engine model. FAS lists Phalanx range as classified, so the 1.8 km engine range and the round count are estimated.

sensors.name: AN/SPY-1D phased-array radar
sensors.role: Aegis air search and track, four fixed arrays on the deckhouse, tracks hundreds of targets at once

sensors.name: AN/SPS-67(V)3 surface search radar
sensors.role: Surface search and navigation, picks out ships and low flyers

sensors.name: AN/SPG-62 fire control radars (3)
sensors.role: Illuminates the target for semi-active SM-2 missiles in the last seconds of flight

sensors.name: AN/SQS-53C bow sonar
sensors.role: Hull-mounted active and passive search for submarines

sensors.name: AN/SQR-19 towed array
sensors.role: Passive long-range listening for submarines on a cable towed behind the ship

sensors.name: AN/SLQ-32(V)3 electronic support
sensors.role: Detects, identifies and bears on hostile radars

sensors.name: Bridge and lookout watch
sensors.role: Eyes and binoculars from the bridge and weather decks

radar.note: The DDG 51 was the first US Navy ship designed with hull shaping to cut radar cross-section, but it is still a 154 m steel ship.

infrared.note: Four gas turbines put out a strong exhaust plume, so the ship shows up clearly to heat-seeking sensors at close range.

acoustic.note: Gas turbine ships are louder than diesel-electric types, and the towed array and bow sonar make her an active participant in the underwater fight.

visual.note: A 154 m grey hull with a tall deckhouse is easy to see on a clear day, but it shows a low profile from a distance.

brief.whatItIs: The Flight II Arleigh Burke is a 154 m US Navy guided-missile destroyer. It carries the Aegis combat system, whose four fixed radar arrays track hundreds of air targets at once and steer long-range Standard missiles onto them. USS Mahan was the first Flight II ship and is the example used here.
brief.howItIsUsed: A commander uses it as the air-defence anchor of a task group. It sits between the carrier or the convoy and the threat axis and keeps the SPY-1D radar on full power so incoming aircraft and missiles are picked up early. The Standard missiles, which need the three SPG-62 illuminators in the final seconds, are the main reach. Harpoon missiles give it an anti-ship punch of its own, and the 5-inch gun and Phalanx deal with small boats and leakers. Its weakness is magazine depth: the 90 vertical cells hold only so many missiles, and a swarm of cheap boats or drones can burn them faster than the ship can reload at sea. Mahan fired warning shots at IRGC boats in the Strait of Hormuz in January 2017, which is the kind of close encounter the ship's guns and lookouts are for.
typicalMissions: Air and missile defence of a carrier or convoy
Anti-surface warfare and maritime security patrol
Anti-submarine escort with towed array and helicopter
Presence and escort in the Strait of Hormuz
